title: Connor Green and Anna Hursey win WTT Contender Istanbul mixed doubles title
seo_title: WTT Contender Istanbul: Green and Hursey win mixed title
description: Connor Green and Anna Hursey beat Evgeny Tikhonov and Maria Panfilova 3-0 for the WTT Contender Istanbul mixed doubles title as the singles finals are set.
standfirst: The British pair saved four game points in the second game of a 3-0 win, while Fang Bo meets Kang Dongsoo and Honoka Hashimoto plays Joo Cheonhui in Sunday's singles finals.

Connor Green and Anna Hursey v Lim Yunoh and Joo Cheonhui, mixed doubles semi-final

body: England's Connor Green and Wales's Anna Hursey won the mixed doubles title at WTT Contender Istanbul on Saturday, beating Russia's Evgeny Tikhonov and Maria Panfilova 11-7, 12-10, 11-9 in 26 minutes in the first final of the week.

It is the first WTT title above Feeder level for either player. The third seeds had lost the first two games of their quarter-final and needed a fifth game to [get past Lim Yunoh and Joo Cheonhui](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-connor-green-anna-hursey-mixed-doubles-final.html) in the semi-finals, but they did not drop a game in the final.
## Six points in a row
The final turned in the second game. Tikhonov and Panfilova, the fourth seeds, led 10-6 and had four game points to level the match. Green and Hursey won the next six points to take it 12-10.

They had come from behind in the first game too, trailing 6-4 before winning seven of the last eight points. In the third they led 8-2 and reached match point at 10-6; the Russians saved three of them before the British pair closed it out 11-9.

Green, 20 and ranked 118th in the world, went out in singles qualifying on Wednesday, and Hursey, the world No 38, lost to the top seed, Honoka Hashimoto, in the singles last 16 on Friday. Their previous titles came on the Feeder circuit: Green won the WTT Feeder Düsseldorf mixed doubles this year with Ho Tin-Tin, beating Hursey and Norway's Borgar Haug in the final, and Hursey won the women's singles at WTT Feeder Manchester in 2025.
## Hashimoto and Joo set up a final between the top seeds

The women's singles final on Sunday is between the top two seeds. Hashimoto, the world No 14 and one of the few choppers left near the top of the women's game, beat her Japanese teammate Miu Hirano 11-8, 11-4, 9-11, 15-13. Hirano, who had [knocked out China's Zong Geman](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-quarter-finals-hirano-yoshiyama-china-out.html) in the morning, saved four match points in the fourth game, the last of them at 13-12, before Hashimoto won the next two points.

South Korea's Joo Cheonhui, the second seed and world No 17, beat Japan's Kaho Akae 11-6, 16-14, 12-10 in 38 minutes. It was closer than the score suggests: Akae, 22 and ranked 37th, led by five points in the second game and had two game points in it, and another at 10-9 in the third.

Hashimoto leads their head-to-head 2-1. She won their quarter-final at WTT Star Contender Chennai in March 2025 and beat Joo 3-0 in the semi-finals of WTT Contender Lagos in May, while Joo won their seven-game quarter-final at WTT Champions Montpellier last year. Hashimoto also plays in Sunday's women's doubles final, with Miyu Nagasaki against Miyuu Kihara and Hirano.
## Two players in their 30s in the men's final

The men's final is between two unseeded players in their 30s. Kazakhstan's Fang Bo, 34 and ranked 160th, came from two games down to beat Germany's Ricardo Walther, also 34, 6-11, 8-11, 11-6, 11-5, 11-1. Fang won the first 10 points of the decider, and Walther's timeout at 3-0 did nothing to stop him.

Fang, the runner-up to Ma Long at the 2015 World Championships, is in his first WTT singles final since [returning to the tour for Kazakhstan](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-qualifying-ends-quadri-aruna-borgar-haug-main-draw.html) this year.

He plays South Korea's Kang Dongsoo, 32 and ranked 120th, who beat Japan's Ryoichi Yoshiyama 12-10, 14-16, 11-4, 9-11, 11-8 in 46 minutes. Kang saved four game points in the first game, winning six points in a row from 10-6 down, and led 10-7 in the decider before taking his second match point. Yoshiyama, 22, had knocked out the second seed, Thibault Poret, and the fifth seed, Li Tianyang, and Kang the third seed, Elias Ranefur, so none of the men's seeds reached the semi-finals.
## Saturday's results

- Mixed doubles, final: Connor Green / Anna Hursey (ENG/WAL) bt Evgeny Tikhonov / Maria Panfilova (RUS) 11-7, 12-10, 11-9
- Women's singles, semi-finals: Honoka Hashimoto (JPN) bt Miu Hirano (JPN) 11-8, 11-4, 9-11, 15-13; Joo Cheonhui (KOR) bt Kaho Akae (JPN) 11-6, 16-14, 12-10
- Men's singles, semi-finals: Fang Bo (KAZ) bt Ricardo Walther (GER) 6-11, 8-11, 11-6, 11-5, 11-1; Kang Dongsoo (KOR) bt Ryoichi Yoshiyama (JPN) 12-10, 14-16, 11-4, 9-11, 11-8
## Finals day
The four remaining finals are on Sunday, all on WTT's YouTube channel, with live scores on Eleven's [event page](/events/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026.html#matches).

- 11am UK: Honoka Hashimoto / Miyu Nagasaki (JPN) v Miyuu Kihara / Miu Hirano (JPN), women's doubles final
- 11.45am: Nikita Artemenko / Maksim Grebnev (RUS) v Luka Mladenovic / Mael Van Dessel (LUX), men's doubles final
- 12.30pm: Kang Dongsoo (KOR) v Fang Bo (KAZ), men's singles final
- 1.15pm: Honoka Hashimoto (JPN) v Joo Cheonhui (KOR), women's singles final
Times are approximate, and Saturday's programme ran later than scheduled.
